trigger: an operator enables RBAC on one replica while a different replica's periodic durable-generation refresh concurrently fails (pool timeout / query error)
summary: maybe_refresh_generation's 'never touch rbac_enabled_ on a read error' contract reasons only about the true->false fail-open direction (per its own comment) -- a replica cached false that never observed a remote enable stays cached false, and rbac_enforcement_in_effect() (the World-A confinement chokepoint) returned false right along with it, for the duration of any refresh outage after the durable flag genuinely flipped true elsewhere. Found independently by both external models (adversarial-review, whole-PR-vs-dev run) and confirmed via my own line-by-line read + CLAUDE.md severity derivation (I1 base HIGH, E5 no cap).
classification_rationale: ADR-0041 'a failed generation refresh must NOT extend trust' -- code honored this for perm_cache_ but not for rbac_enabled_.

summary: Fixed in f8bbb06db: new RbacStore::rbac_enabled_view_degraded() accessor; rbac_enforcement_in_effect() treats a degraded generation view the same as enabled. Raw is_rbac_enabled() unchanged (its other non-confinement callers rely on the raw value). New test reproduces the real production code path (genuine pool-starvation timeout, not a mock); confirmed red against pre-fix code via git-stash isolation, then green. Full [rbac_store] suite (80/80) and full server suite (4/4 shards) green.

seed_defaults()'s grant() lambda commits new role_permissions rows without calling bump_generation_in_txn, unlike every other mutator (set_permission, assign_role, etc). Failure direction is stale-deny (a replica with a cached deny for a newly-seeded default grant keeps denying until an unrelated write or restart), not stale-allow -- availability, not security. Both models agree LOW.
classification_rationale: ADR-0041 requires every mutation to bump the durable counter in the same txn; this one doesn't.

summary: Not actioned this round -- LOW, stale-deny-only, self-heals on restart, not gating. Flagged to the operator for a filing decision rather than filed unilaterally, per the same standing pattern as prior LOW should-fix items this branch.

trigger: a partial RBAC/EnginePrincipalStore Postgres read failure while other reference tables still read
summary: The engine-principal no-admin auditor (REST + MCP) uses bare-vector RBAC/EnginePrincipalStore accessors that fail-open (empty) on error, indistinguishable from genuinely-empty -- the route's own comment already admits this, and docs/auth-architecture.md's 'No-admin auditor' section explicitly promises a 503 instead. Confirmed real and HIGH via direct code read. NOT this PR's own defect: rest_api_v1.cpp/mcp_server.cpp/engine_principal_store.cpp have zero lines touched by this PR's diff (verified via git diff --stat origin/dev...HEAD), and the exact same fail-open shape exists verbatim in the pre-migration SQLite list_roles() (verified via git show at the merge-base) -- this PR ported an existing accessor behavior unchanged, it did not introduce the gap.
classification_rationale: Doc explicitly promises 503; code does not deliver it for 3 of 5 reads.
